rows.algorithm: Format and parse back n signed 64-bit integers and n doubles with the language's std formatting and parsing (shortest round-trip digits for the doubles where the std has them); rounds times (README.md).
notes: B18: C's std has no shortest round-trip float format, so the c cell prints %.17g (round-trips, but longer output than the other columns: not the same work); mk, rust, zig and go print the shortest round-trip digits.
Checksum: the wrapping sum of every parsed integer and of every parsed double truncated toward zero, plus the number of doubles that parsed back bit-exact (n per round when every format round-trips).

skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; formatting has no arithmetic to wrap

rows.algorithm: Hash map churn with each language's standard map and its default hash, u64 keys: n splitmix64-mixed keys inserted into a map that grows from empty, each looked up once with a hit and once with a miss, every other key removed, all n looked up again; rounds times with a fresh map (README.md; the std-hash lane's maphash task).
notes: Hashes and DoS posture (B20): mk Map.New, DD-5's fast fixed hash, public key; mk-keyed Map.NewKeyed, SipHash-1-3 under a random per-process key; Rust HashMap, SipHash-1-3 under RandomState's random key; Zig AutoHashMap, wyhash-based autoHash with seed 0, fixed; Go map, AES-based runtime hash seeded per map.
The same task as tests/bench-lanes/std-hash/maphash, with the checksums that lane recorded; this row adds the mk-keyed column B20 asks for.
